metadata.title: Gender, mindset, and teacher support predict students’ math motivation profiles: Evidence from five countries in PISA 2022

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: The study used PISA 2022 student microdata for 15-year-olds from Finland, Germany, Japan, Korea, and the United States, recruited via a stratified two-stage sampling design. In all analyses, the authors included the final student weight W_FSTUWT provided by OECD to account for unequal selection probabilities and to adjust sampling variance so estimates better generalize to the target populations. The paper does not report replicate-weight methods (e.g., BRR/jackknife), and it does not describe any additional weight calibration beyond W_FSTUWT. Because the main modeling approach is latent profile analysis in Mplus (with FIML for missingness and PV-based achievement contrasts via multiple imputations), the weighting is applied at the estimation stage rather than as a separate ML training weight.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: Used PISA 2022 student data for 15-year-olds in the five specified countries (Finland, Germany, Japan, Korea, United States). The analytic sample includes students aged 15 in PISA 2022, which correspond to grade levels ranging from Grade 7 to Grade 12 (most in Grades 9–10). The study used PISA 2022 ready-made index variables for motivation indicators; for variables based on the within-construct matrix sampling design, responses were scaled into weighted likelihood estimates (WLE). For math achievement outcomes, the authors used the PV-based achievement data (imputed as 10 plausible values) and did not restrict to a single grade band beyond the PISA 15-year-old target population.

main_findings.dataset_used: PISA 2022 (15-year-olds) Mathematics motivation profiles (WLE indicators) — Finland, Germany, Japan, Korea, United States
main_findings.performance_metrics: Not reported as a single ML metric; profile differences tested via Wald tests and reported as significant with Bonferroni-corrected p < .003 (Table 2). Additional analysis (Time spent on math homework (profile outcome means)): Not reported as a single ML metric; profile differences tested via Wald tests with Bonferroni-corrected p < .003 (Table 2). Additional analysis (Math achievement (PV-based profile outcome means)): Not reported as a single ML metric; achievement contrasts used 10 plausible values with multiple imputations and profile differences tested via Wald tests with Bonferroni-corrected p < .003 (Table 2).
main_findings.standardized_conclusion: Using PISA 2022 the study leveraged gender, fixed mindset, and teacher support/practices to examine math motivation latent profile membership and its association with math classroom engagement, finding that the highly motivated profile showed the highest engagement while unmotivated profiles showed the lowest engagement across all five countries. This indicates that strengthening students’ math confidence and supportive instructional conditions may help shift learners toward more adaptive motivation profiles that are linked to greater classroom engagement, though the cross-sectional design limits causal claims.

data.outcome_summary: This study used PISA 2022 student microdata for 15-year-olds in Finland, Germany, Japan, Korea, and the United States (total N=27,421) to identify math motivation latent profiles based on WLE-scaled indicators of self-efficacy, anxiety, intrinsic value, and attainment value. The authors estimated latent profile models in Mplus (MLR with robust SEs and FIML for missingness) and then compared profile means for four math outcomes: classroom engagement, math homework time, STEM career intention, and math achievement. Achievement contrasts were computed using 10 plausible values with multiple imputations, and profile differences were tested with Wald tests (Bonferroni-corrected p < .003). The highly motivated profile consistently showed the most favorable outcomes, while unmotivated profiles showed the least favorable outcomes, with cross-national exceptions for the mixed profile. Limitations include cross-sectional design (no causal inference) and reliance on single-item measures for intrinsic and attainment value.
data.null_fields_interpretation: Although the paper is included in a search context related to machine learning, the empirical analysis is person-centered latent profile analysis (LPA) rather than supervised predictive ML. Therefore, no ML algorithms (e.g., Random Forest, XGBoost) are trained or evaluated, and ml_techniques is intentionally left empty. The study’s key outputs are profile solutions (AIC/BIC/SABIC, entropy, LMR tests) and profile-outcome mean differences, which are not ML performance metrics.
